Rates and assessment

EMPLOYEES' OLD﷓AGE BENEFITS ACT, 1976
EMPLOYEES' OLD‑AGE BENEFITS ACT, 1976
Act No. XIV of 1976
[April, 15, 1976]
An Act
to repeal and re‑enact the law relating to old‑age benefits
for the persons employed in industrial, commercial and other organisations.
CHAPTER III
CONTRIBUTIONS
9. Rates and assessment. ‑‑
(1) On and form the first day of
July, 1976, contributions shall be payable every month by the employer to tire
Institution in respect of every person in his insurable employment, at the rate
of five percent of his wages in the prescribed manner;
(Proviso added by Ord. XVII of 1983=1983
PLS 81.)[Provided that no
contribution shall be payable on so much of an insured person's wages as in
excess of [three thousand](Subs. for "one thousand five hundred" by s. 8(2) of
the Labour Law (Amendment) Act, 1994. Gaz. of Pak. Extr. Pt. 1, June 29, 1994,
p. 224‑235. Earlier it was subs. for "one thousand" by Act XVI
of 1985, Schedule.) rupees];
()[Provided further that no contribution shall payable in respect
of an insured person who is in receipt of pension under this Act or has
attained the age of sixty‑years, or fifty‑five years in the case of
a woman) (Subs.
by Finance Act (Act 1 of 1986), s. 11(4); Gaz. of Pak., Extr., Pt. I, June 29,
1986.) [;]
(Third proviso inserted by the Labour Laws
(Amendment) Ordinance, 2001 (Ord. LIII of 2001), s. 7(3) (effective
retrospectively from July 1 2001); Gaz. of Pak. Extr. Pt. I, October 6, 2001,
p. 1475‑1481. [See also EASTERN
WORKER, Vol. 41, No. 5, 3 Sept.‑Oct., 2001].) [Provided also that in case an employer
opts for a self assessment scheme, no contribution shall be payable on so much
of an insured persons wages as is in excess of five thousand rupees.]
(2) Where any insured person does
not receive any wages from the employer for any period, the Institution shall,
subject to regulations, determine the amount of wages with reference to which
the contributions shall be computed.
(3) Notwithstanding any agreement
to the contrary, the employer shall not deduct from the wages of an insured
person or otherwise recover from him any portion of contribution.
(4) Where the mode of payment of
remuneration, whether in cash or in kind, makes it difficult to determine the
amount of wages for computing the contribution, the Institution may, subject to
regulations, determine such wages.
COMMENTARY
Since 1994 amendment, the
employee's wage limit has been Rs. 3000 per month on which contributions are
payable at the rate of five percent (5%) [first proviso of section 9(1) above].
Hence, the maximum contribution for every employee has been be Rs. 150 per
month (Rs. 3000. x 5 %).
However, if an employer opts for
a self assessment scheme, introduced in 2001 [third proviso of section 9(1)],
higher wage limit of Rs. 5000 pm would apply instead of Rs. 3000 pm, on which
contribution (Rs. 250 pm) shall be payable. In return, the benefit gained by
employer would be no inspection of its records and returns for a period of two
years under section 2 amended clause (oa) [definition of self assessment
scheme), and section 12(1), amended clause (c).

Registration of establishments etc

Act No. XIV of 1976
[April, 15, 1976]
An Act
to repeal and re‑enact the law relating to old‑age benefits
for the persons employed in industrial, commercial and other organisations.
CHAPTER III
CONTRIBUTIONS
11. Registration of establishment, etc.‑‑
(1) Every employer shall before
the expiration of thirty days from the day on which this Act becomes applicable
to the industry or establishment in respect of which he is the employer,
communicate to the Institution the name and other prescribed particulars of the
Industry or establishment and of every insured person employed in the industry
or establishment.
(2) Every insured person may also
communicate his name and other prescribed particulars to the Institution.
(3) On receipt of a communication
under sub‑section (1) or sub‑section (2), the Institution shall
register the name of the industry or establishment or the insured person in
such manner, and issue to the insured person a registration card in such form,
as may be prescribed.
COMMENTARY
It is the responsibility of the
employer to find out whether the Act is applicable to it or not and register
itself with the Institution if the answer is in affirmative. Such legal
obligation having not been discharged by establishment, Institution was free to
press into service provisions of S. 12 of the Act to verify the employer
assertion of non‑applicability of Act to itself. Held, establishment was,
thus, not entitled to relief in Constitutional jurisdiction which was dismissed
in circumstances [H.C. (Lah.): Lahore Race Club vs. Deputy Director, EOBI; 1995
PLC 494].

Officials of institution to check employer's books

(3) If an employer fail to

Increase of unpaid contribution and recovery of contribution etc as arrears of land revenue

EMPLOYEES' OLD﷓AGE BENEFITS ACT, 1976
EMPLOYEES' OLD‑AGE BENEFITS ACT, 1976
Act No. XIV of 1976
[April, 15, 1976]
An Act
to repeal and re‑enact the law relating to old‑age benefits
for the persons employed in industrial, commercial and other organisations.
CHAPTER III
CONTRIBUTIONS
13. Increase of unpaid contribution and recovery of contribution, etc.,
as arrears of land revenue. ‑‑
(1) If an
employer fails to pay on the due date, the contribution payable by him under
sub‑section (1) of section 9, the amount so payable by him shall be increased
by such percentage or amount as may be prescribed.
Provided that no case shall such
increase exceed fifty percent of the amount due.
(2) Without prejudice to any
other remedy, the amount of the contribution due, together with the increase
provided for under sub‑section (1), as may be recovered as an arrear of
land revenue.
COMMENTARY
Absence of determination of
contribution is no excuse to avoid paying penalty for being late in payment.
Employer who fail to pay contribution in time had contended that since amount
of contribution was not determined, he could not be made to pay late fee and
that in absence of determination penalty of 50 % could not be imposed on him.
This contention was rejected in view of the fact that liability to pay
contribution was automatic and change was created by law unconnected with any
proceedings for determination of same. Penalty provision, however, would be
attracted even after if there was no will default in payment of contribution
[H.C. (Lah.): Avari Hotel Ltd. vs. Employees Old‑Age Benefits Institution
and others, 1994 PLC 688].
